questions.stem:
The point $P$ lies on the curve with equation
$y = 4\mathrm{e}^{2x+1}$.
The $y$-coordinate of $P$ is 8.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find, in terms of $\ln 2$, the $x$-coordinate of $P$.
(2)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point $P$ in the form $y=ax+b$, where $a$ and $b$ are exact constants to be found.
(4)

questions.question_text:
The point $P$ lies on the curve with equation
$y = 4\mathrm{e}^{2x+1}$.
The $y$-coordinate of $P$ is 8.
(a) Find, in terms of $\ln 2$, the $x$-coordinate of $P$.
(2)
(b) Find the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point $P$ in the form $y=ax+b$, where $a$ and $b$ are exact constants to be found.
(4)
questions.mark_scheme_text:
(a) $\mathrm{e}^{2x+1}=2$ M1: forming this equation
$2x+1=\ln 2$
$x=\frac{1}{2}(\ln 2-1)$ A1 (2)
(b) $\frac{dy}{dx}=8\mathrm{e}^{2x+1}$ B1
$x=\frac{1}{2}(\ln 2-1) \Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx}=16$ B1
$y-8=16\left(x-\frac{1}{2}(\ln 2-1)\right)$ M1
$y=16x+16-8\ln 2$ A1 (4)
[6]

Given that $\mathrm{f}(x)=R\cos(x-\alpha)$, where $R>0$ and $0<\alpha<\frac{\pi}{2}$,

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) find the value of $R$ and the value of $\alpha$ to 3 decimal places.
(4)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Hence solve the equation
$5\cos x+12\sin x=6$
for $0\leqslant x<2\pi$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $\cos(x-\alpha)=\frac{6}{13}$ M1
$x-\alpha=\arccos\frac{6}{13}=1.091\ldots$ A1
$x=1.091\ldots+1.176\ldots\approx 2.267\ldots$ awrt 2.3 A1
$x-\alpha=-1.091\ldots$ (accept $\ldots=5.19\ldots$ for M) M1
$x=-1.091\ldots+1.176\ldots\approx 0.0849\ldots$ awrt 0.084 or 0.085 A1 (5)

parts.label: c(i)
parts.text:
(c) (i) Write down the maximum value of $5\cos x+12\sin x$.
(1)

parts.label: c(ii)

(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(ii) At the maximum, $\cos(x-\alpha)=1$ or $x-\alpha=0$ M1
$x=\alpha=1.176\ldots$ awrt 1.2, ft their $\alpha$ A1ft (2)

The graph cuts the $y$-axis at the point $Q$ and the $x$-axis at the points $(-3,0)$ and $R$.

questions.stem:
The function f is defined by
$\mathrm{f}: x \mapsto \frac{2(x-1)}{x^2-2x-3}-\frac{1}{x-3}, \quad x>3.$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Show that $\mathrm{f}(x)=\frac{1}{x+1}, \quad x>3$.
(4)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the range of f.
(2)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find $\mathrm{f}^{-1}(x)$. State the domain of this inverse function.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) Let $y=\mathrm{f}(x)$: $y=\frac{1}{x+1}$
$x=\frac{1}{y+1}$
$yx+x=1$
$y=\frac{1-x}{x}$ (or $\frac{1}{x}-1$) M1 A1
$\mathrm{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{1-x}{x}$
Domain of $\mathrm{f}^{-1}$ is $\left(0,\frac{1}{4}\right)$ ft their part (b) B1ft (3)

parts.label: d
parts.text:
The function g is defined by
$\mathrm{g}: x \mapsto 2x^2-3, \quad x\in\mathbb{R}.$
(d) Solve $\mathrm{fg}(x)=\frac{1}{8}$.
(3)

questions.question_text:
The function f is defined by
$\mathrm{f}: x \mapsto \frac{2(x-1)}{x^2-2x-3}-\frac{1}{x-3}, \quad x>3.$
(a) Show that $\mathrm{f}(x)=\frac{1}{x+1}, \quad x>3$.
(4)
(b) Find the range of f.
(2)
(c) Find $\mathrm{f}^{-1}(x)$. State the domain of this inverse function.
(3)
The function g is defined by
$\mathrm{g}: x \mapsto 2x^2-3, \quad x\in\mathbb{R}.$
(d) Solve $\mathrm{fg}(x)=\frac{1}{8}$.
(3)
questions.mark_scheme_text:
(a) $x^2-2x-3=(x-3)(x+1)$ B1
$\mathrm{f}(x)=\frac{2(x-1)-(x+1)}{(x-3)(x+1)}$ (or $\frac{2(x-1)}{(x-3)(x+1)}-\frac{x+1}{(x-3)(x+1)}$) M1 A1
$=\frac{x-3}{(x-3)(x+1)}=\frac{1}{x+1}$ * cso A1 (4)
(b) $\left(0,\frac{1}{4}\right)$ Accept $0<y<\frac{1}{4}$, $0<\mathrm{f}(x)<\frac{1}{4}$ etc. B1 B1 (2)
(c) Let $y=\mathrm{f}(x)$: $y=\frac{1}{x+1}$
$x=\frac{1}{y+1}$
$yx+x=1$
$y=\frac{1-x}{x}$ (or $\frac{1}{x}-1$) M1 A1
$\mathrm{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{1-x}{x}$
Domain of $\mathrm{f}^{-1}$ is $\left(0,\frac{1}{4}\right)$ ft their part (b) B1ft (3)
(d) $\mathrm{fg}(x)=\frac{1}{2x^2-3+1}$
$\frac{1}{2x^2-2}=\frac{1}{8}$ M1
$x^2=5$ A1
$x=\pm\sqrt{5}$ both A1 (3)
[12]

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Given that $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta \equiv 1$, show that $1+\cot^2\theta \equiv \mathrm{cosec}^2\theta$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1$
$\div\sin^2\theta$: $\frac{\sin^2\theta}{\sin^2\theta}+\frac{\cos^2\theta}{\sin^2\theta}=\frac{1}{\sin^2\theta}$ M1
$1+\cot^2\theta=\mathrm{cosec}^2\theta$ * cso A1 (2)
Alternative for (a): $1+\cot^2\theta=1+\frac{\cos^2\theta}{\sin^2\theta}=\frac{\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta}{\sin^2\theta}=\frac{1}{\sin^2\theta}$ M1
$=\mathrm{cosec}^2\theta$ * cso A1

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Solve, for $0\leqslant \theta<180^\circ$, the equation
$2\cot^2\theta-9\mathrm{cosec}\,\theta=3$,
giving your answers to 1 decimal place.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $2(\mathrm{cosec}^2\theta-1)-9\mathrm{cosec}\,\theta=3$ M1
$2\mathrm{cosec}^2\theta-9\mathrm{cosec}\,\theta-5=0$ or $5\sin^2\theta+9\sin\theta-2=0$ M1
$(2\mathrm{cosec}\,\theta+1)(\mathrm{cosec}\,\theta-5)=0$ or $(5\sin\theta-1)(\sin\theta+2)=0$ M1
$\mathrm{cosec}\,\theta=5$ or $\sin\theta=\frac{1}{5}$ A1
$\theta=11.5^\circ, 168.5^\circ$ A1 A1 (6)
[8]

questions.question_text:
$\mathrm{f}(x)=3x^3-2x-6$
(a) Show that $\mathrm{f}(x)=0$ has a root, $\alpha$, between $x=1.4$ and $x=1.45$
(2)
(b) Show that the equation $\mathrm{f}(x)=0$ can be written as
$x=\sqrt{\left(\frac{2}{x}+\frac{2}{3}\right)}, \quad x\neq 0$.
(3)
(c) Starting with $x_0=1.43$, use the iteration
$x_{n+1}=\sqrt{\left(\frac{2}{x_n}+\frac{2}{3}\right)}$
to calculate the values of $x_1$, $x_2$ and $x_3$, giving your answers to 4 decimal places.
(3)
(d) By choosing a suitable interval, show that $\alpha=1.435$ is correct to 3 decimal places.
(3)
questions.mark_scheme_text:
(a) $\mathrm{f}(1.4)=-0.568\ldots<0$
$\mathrm{f}(1.45)=0.245\ldots>0$ M1
Change of sign (and continuity) $\Rightarrow \alpha\in(1.4,1.45)$ A1 (2)
(b) $3x^3=2x+6$
$x^3=\frac{2x}{3}+2$
$x^2=\frac{2}{3}+\frac{2}{x}$ M1 A1
$x=\sqrt{\left(\frac{2}{x}+\frac{2}{3}\right)}$ * cso A1 (3)
(c) $x_1=1.4371$ B1
$x_2=1.4347$ B1
$x_3=1.4355$ B1 (3)
(d) Choosing the interval $(1.4345,1.4355)$ or appropriate tighter interval. M1
$\mathrm{f}(1.4345)=-0.01\ldots$ M1
$\mathrm{f}(1.4355)=0.003\ldots$
Change of sign (and continuity) $\Rightarrow \alpha\in(1.4345,1.4355)$
$\Rightarrow \alpha=1.435$, correct to 3 decimal places * cso A1 (3)
[11]
Note: $\alpha=1.435304553\ldots$
